metadata.title: Strict $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-triangulation of subanalytic sets in low dimensions
metadata.abstract: Let $R$ be a real closed field expanded by an o-minimal structure, let $A$ be a definable, closed and bounded subset of $R^n$ and let $p$ be a positive integer. It was recently shown in \cite{pa2} that $A$ admits a strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation $({\mathcal T},h)$, i.e., there exist a finite simplicial complex ${\mathcal T}$ in $R^n$ and a homeomorphism $h:|{\mathcal T}|\to A$ that is definable and of class ${\mathcal C}^p$. The aim of this article is to analyze a generalization of the notion of strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation of subanalytic sets to the case $p=\infty$. Examples in dimension $n=3$ show that such a generalization is not always possible within subanalytic geometry, where the class ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ is equivalent to the class ${\mathcal C}^\omega$. We formulate the conjecture that strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulations of subanalytic sets always exist in the wider o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, generated by subanalytic sets and the exponential function. We check the conjecture for all subanalytic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n\leq 3$, and prepare tools to address the conjecture for arbitrary $n$. We also apply the obtained strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulation results to approximate subanalytic continuous mappings $f:X\to Y$ between subanalytic sets $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-mappings $g:X\to Y$ definable in the o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, with respect to the strong Whitney ${\mathcal C}^0$ topology. If the continuous mapping $f:X\to Y$ is not necessarily subanalytic, we can still approximate it by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ mappings $g:X\to Y$.
